t.3.50.1: The lord of the Rākṣasas saw that vulture, his life nearly spent, fallen upon the ground near Rāghava's hermitage, quivering.
t.3.50.2: But she, whose face was like the lord of the stars, seeing that king of vultures struck down by Rāvaṇa, lamented, deeply grieved.
t.3.50.3: Omens, the knowledge of signs, and the sight and cries of birds are invariably seen to appear to men in times of joy and sorrow.
t.3.50.4: Surely, O Rāma, you do not know the great calamity that has befallen you; surely, O Kākutstha, the beasts and birds are running about for my sake.
t.3.50.6: Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, rushed upon Vaidehī as she lamented like one without a protector, her garlands and ornaments crushed and disordered.
t.3.50.5: "Save me now, Kākutstha! Lakṣmaṇa!" So the lovely lady, utterly terrified, cried out, as if to those who could hear her close at hand.
t.3.50.8: She was crying out "Rāma, Rāma!" in the forest, bereft of Rāma, when he who resembled Antaka, the god of death, seized her by the hair to bring her life to an end.
t.3.50.7: Her, who was twining like a creeper and clinging to the great trees, the lord of the rākṣasas, crying out again and again, "Let go, let go!"…
t.3.50.9: When Vaidehī was violated, the whole world with all its moving and unmoving beings became lawless, enveloped in blinding darkness.
t.3.50.10: Seeing with his divine eye the wretched Sītā seized, the glorious Grandsire declared, "The deed is done!"
t.3.50.11: Seeing Sītā seized, all those supreme sages dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest were at once delighted and distressed.
t.3.50.12: But Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, seized her as she wept, crying "Rāma, Rāma!" and "Lakṣmaṇa!", and carried her off into the sky.
t.3.50.13: Her every limb adorned with ornaments of burnished gold and clad in yellow silk, the princess shone like a flash of lightning.
t.3.50.14: And with her yellow garment fluttering upward about him, Rāvaṇa shone all the more brightly, like a mountain set ablaze by fire.
t.3.50.16: Her golden-hued silk garment, tossed up into the sky, shone like a coppery cloud in the sunshine, reddened by the glow of the sun.
t.3.50.15: The coppery and fragrant lotus petals of that most auspicious lady were scattered by Vaidehī all over Rāvaṇa.
t.3.50.17: That spotless face of hers, resting in the sky on Rāvaṇa's lap, did not shine without Rāma, like a lotus without its stalk.
t.3.50.18: Her face, with its fine forehead and lovely hairline, glowing like the heart of a lotus, flawless, and adorned with white, spotless, gleaming teeth, became like the moon that has risen after breaking through a dark cloud.
t.3.50.19: Her face, weeping, its tears wiped away, lovely to behold like the moon, with its fine nose and beautiful coppery lips, gleamed in the sky with the radiance of gold.
t.3.50.21: That golden-hued Maithilī, clinging to the dark-limbed lord of the rākṣasas, shone like a golden girdle set upon a dark sapphire.
t.3.50.20: That auspicious speech of hers, shaken by the lord of the rākṣasas, did not shine without Rāma, like the moon risen in the daytime.
t.3.50.22: Janaka's daughter, fair as a lotus and radiant as gold, adorned with ornaments of refined gold, shone as she clung to Rāvaṇa, like lightning entering a dark cloud.
t.3.50.23: With the jingling of the ornaments of Vaidehī, the lord of the rākṣasas became like a clear, dark cloud rumbling with thunder.
t.3.50.24: As Sītā was being carried away, a shower of flowers slipped from her head and fell all around upon the surface of the earth.
t.3.50.25: But that shower of flowers, scattered all around by the force of Rāvaṇa's speed, fell back once more upon Daśagrīva himself.
t.3.50.26: A stream of flowers fell upon the younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa, like a garland of stars, spotless and bright, descending upon Meru, the loftiest of mountains.
t.3.50.27: Slipping from Vaidehī's foot, her anklet, adorned with jewels and gleaming like a ring of lightning, fell with a sweet tinkling sound.
t.3.50.29: Entering the sky, the younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa carried off Sītā, who blazed with her own radiance like a great meteor in the heavens.
t.3.50.28: Vaidehī, reddish like the tender shoots of a tree, made the dark-limbed lord of the rākṣasas shine, as a golden girth adorns an elephant.
t.3.50.30: Her fire-coloured ornaments scattered with a jingling sound upon the surface of the earth, like waning stars falling from the sky.
t.3.50.31: Slipping from between her breasts and falling away from Vaidehī, the necklace, radiant as the lord of the stars, shone like the Gaṅgā descending from the sky.
t.3.50.32: The trees, struck by the winds of ill omen and thronged with flocks of many kinds of birds, their tops shaking, seemed to cry out, "Do not be afraid!"
t.3.50.34: Then lions, tigers, deer and birds, rushing together from every side, ran in anger after Sītā's shadow, following it as it moved.
t.3.50.33: The lotus ponds, their lotuses ruined and their fish and water creatures terrified, seemed to grieve for Maithilī as if for a friend who had lost all heart.
t.3.50.35: As Sītā was being carried away, the mountains, their faces streaming with tears in the form of waterfalls and their peaks raised like uplifted arms, seemed to cry aloud in lament.
t.3.50.36: But seeing Vaidehī being carried off, the glorious sun grew dejected; its radiance was shattered and its orb turned pale.
t.3.50.37: There is no righteousness, so how can there be truth? There is no uprightness, no compassion, where Rāvaṇa carries off Vaidehī, the wife of Rāma.
t.3.50.38: Thus all creatures lamented in their multitudes, and the young fawns, terrified and with woeful faces, wept.
t.3.50.39: Gazing up again and again with their eyes, their sight clouded by falling tears, the forest deities stood with their limbs violently trembling.
t.3.50.41: Vaidehī, that high-minded lady, kept gazing again and again at the surface of the earth, the ends of her hair disheveled and the auspicious mark on her brow rubbed away. Daśagrīva carried her off, to his own destruction.
t.3.50.40: Having seen Sītā wailing loudly, fallen thus into sorrow, crying out in her sweet voice, “Lakṣmaṇa! Rāma!”
t.3.50.42: Then Maithilī, she of lovely teeth and pure smile, bereft of her kinsfolk and not seeing either Rāghava or Lakṣmaṇa, grew pale of face, oppressed by the weight of her fear.
